leads.name: Dąb Benedykta XVI, Rudy
leads.blocked_reason: Not a candidate: this is one of the 'papal oaks' (dab papieski), a young sapling grown from acorns of the Chrobry oak that were blessed by John Paul II in April 2004 and distributed to Poland's forest districts in 2006 for planting; a Commons photo of this specimen is already dated 2007-07, consistent with a tree roughly 19-20 years old today, not an ancient or visually spectacular tree. Hundreds of near-identical papal oaks were planted nationwide from the same acorn batch, so it is also not a distinctive collectible point. Fails the qualifying bar (not genuinely old, not visually spectacular; historical significance is shared with hundreds of sibling trees elsewhere). Recorded here rather than silently dropped so a future pass does not re-research it.

leads.name: Trzy Dęby, Kędzierzyn-Koźle
leads.hold_reason: Checked 2026-09-08. No register/GDOS/municipal listing found under this name (Kedzierzyn-Kozle's own BIP page of 53 designated monuments does not list a 'Trzy Deby'). A detailed local-history article (wachtyrz.eu, 'Festung Cosel') describes a different, well-documented set of three oaks on the Kozle riverside promenade (Promenada ks. Rutyny) said by tradition to honour Frederick the Great, compared in an 1899 photo against a 2014-ish present-day photo, but states plainly that 'by 2020 one of the three oaks had completely died and was removed', leaving only two. It is not confirmed whether the geotagged Commons photo (2023-09-16, at 50.33636,18.14681) shows that same promenade site (now down to two survivors, which would make the name 'Three Oaks' false) or a different set of three oaks entirely; no source ties the Commons coordinate to the promenade site or vice versa. Also unresolved: whether the surviving tree(s), if this is the promenade site, are individually remarkable or a collectible point on their own. Needs a pass that can see the photos/site clearly (geolocate the Commons images against the promenade) or find a source naming the exact current count and species before this can verify. Left as a lead rather than blocked, since a real ensemble may still be there under this or another name.

leads.name: Cis pospolity, Park w Strzelcach Opolskich
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.hold_reason: Checked 2026-09-08. Existence confirmed (photo geotag 50.50909,18.30007 matches exactly, CC BY-SA, Fry72, 2023-07-02) but this yew is not individually documented: pl.wikipedia's own article on the park (Park Renardow / Park w Strzelcach Opolskich) speaks only of 'trzystuletnie cisy' (three-hundred-year-old yews, plural) with no girth or exact age for any single specimen, so it does not clear the single-tree-destination test on its own (no source distinguishes THIS yew from its neighbours). The third listed photo (Strzelce Opolskie - Zamek - panoramio.jpg) is a photo of the town castle, not the tree; do not use it. IMPORTANT FINDING for a future pass: the same park (65 ha, English-style, built for Andrzej Renard in the 19th c.) also holds, per the same Wikipedia article, a common spruce (Swierk pospolity) recorded in 1992 as one of the oldest common spruces in Poland, aged 337 years then, girth 490cm at 0.5m height, and the tallest common elm in Poland at 37.5m. Those two, plus this yew and any other pomnik przyrody in the park (the town's own site says the commune holds 9 designated trees/tree groups total), could add up to a genuine 4-tree cluster at this one park without needing the single-tree exception at all. Worth a dedicated Strzelce Opolskie pass rather than shipping this yew alone.

blocked.name: Dąb Jagiełły
blocked.reason: Confirmed DEAD: blown down by a storm on the night of 2 November 1974 (pl.wikipedia's own dedicated article on the tree opens 'martwy dab w Puszczy Bialowieskiej'; corroborated by bpn.com.pl and the Puszcza Bialowieska encyclopedia). Was at most ~450 years old at fall, girth 550cm at 130cm height, height 39m. Only its decomposing trunk remains on public display today, reached by a 4km marked trail 'Do Debu Jagielly'; a single acorn-grown descendant sapling ('Jagiellonczyk') survives in the Bialowieska Geobotanical Station's garden but is a different, young, non-public tree. Never publish the original as a collectible entry per the never-dead-tree rule; the Commons photos in this lead (dated 2016) show the decomposing trunk itself, consistent with the dead status, not a living tree.

blocked.name: Baobab in Lublin
blocked.reason: Not a baobab at all and confirmed GONE: this was a black poplar on Plac Litewski (Lithuanian Square) in central Lublin, over 100 years old, popularly nicknamed 'baobab' by residents for its bulbous trunk shape, never an Adansonia (Wikidata Q9360082 labels it plainly: 'Topola czarna zwana baobabem na placu Litewskim w Lublinie', i.e. 'Black poplar called baobab...'). It was felled by the city on 23 May 2017 on the provincial heritage conservator's recommendation; naszemiasto.pl's detailed retrospective (published 2024-05-23, exactly 7 years later) describes the 2.5-hour felling in front of residents and journalists, and that a UMCS Botanical Garden dendrologist took 100 cuttings beforehand in hope some might one day be replanted on the square. The photo filename in this lead, 'Ostatnia godzina baobabu' ('the baobab's last hour'), documents the felling itself. No living tree at this location to verify or publish; blocked on both grounds (dead since 2017, and never the species its nickname implies).
